#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=brats
#   --time=2:00:00
#   --mem=17GB
#   --ntasks-per-node=4
#   --nodes=1
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --mail-user=
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#   --output=logs/test_brats.txt

#flux: --job-name=brats
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=2h
#flux: --output=logs/test_brats.txt

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=17GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-user / --mail-type
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

# NOTE: Slurm requested 4 tasks, but the training script likely runs as a single process.
# Preserve the allocation and launch under Flux.
flux run -n 1 -c 4 python train_brats.py \
  --dataset="brats" \
  --data_dir="datasets/BraTS" \
  --resume_epoch=-1 \
  --test_epoch=-1 \
  --optimizer="adam" \
  --spatial_size=128 \
  --prune_spatial_size=96 \
  --enable_cuda \
  --width 2 \
  --number_of_fmaps 4 \
  --neuron_sparsity=0.7817 \
  --resource_list_type="grad_flops" \
  --enable_train \
  --valid_spatial_size=192

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 17GB of memory (`--mem=17GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.

The resource section requests 4 tasks with 1 core each (`#flux: -n 4 -c 1`), but the intended execution is 1 task with 4 cores (`flux run -n 1 -c 4`). This is a resource mismatch/overallocation in the allocation request.
